links.outcome: Disclosure of personal details and re-identifiability when a local agent consults remote LLMs
links.effect: Personal-detail disclosure fell from 98.0% to 0.2% of cases versus plain delegation. Cases narrowable to ten or fewer registry patients fell from 74% to 0%. Task accuracy rose by up to 15.8 points.
links.quote: In the same setting, PrivMeSA reduces the disclosure of personal details from 98.0% to 0.2% of cases and the share of cases in which the patient can be narrowed to ten or fewer registry patients from 74% to 0%.

links.outcome: Leakage of identifying information in outbound transcripts to remote LLMs, with and without learned disclosure control
links.effect: The learned disclosure controller cut direct disclosure from 98.0% to 0.2% of cases and registry-based narrowing to ten or fewer patients from 74% to 0%.
links.quote: In the same setting, PrivMeSA reduces the disclosure of personal details from 98.0% to 0.2% of cases and the share of cases in which the patient can be narrowed to ten or fewer registry patients from 74% to 0%.

screen.reason: Evaluates a multi-agent privacy guardrail architecture (PrivMeSA) designed to control and redact quasi-identifiers before delegating clinical queries to remote LLMs.

primary.practice: privacy-aware local-remote delegation and redaction guardrail
